requirement:
The requirements index links to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
The subject has one obligation. The requirements index must link to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter. The parent requirement `requirements.test-coverage.index` says this subchapter is generated under the index whether the index is explicitly placed or automatically generated. The marked tests cover both cases and assert the link text and target directly.

- **Explicitly placed index:** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` uses an index chapter that contains a `{requirements-index}` marker, at `appendix/requirements-index.md`. It asserts that the index content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`. It also asserts that exactly one "Documented coverage gaps" sub-chapter exists, that its path is `appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md`, and that its parent is "Requirements index". The link target therefore matches the generated chapter's location relative to a nested index.
- **Automatically generated default index:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` has no marker, so the index is generated. It asserts the content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`. It also asserts a single coverage sub-chapter at `requirements-index/coverage.md` whose parent is "Requirements index".
- **Index in a different book location:** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` puts the index at `reports.md`, under a "Reports" parent. It asserts the parent content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)`. It runs this both with and without a section number, and also checks the generated chapter's path and hierarchy.

I found no plausible violation these tests would accept. If the link were omitted, or pointed at the wrong relative path, at least one of these assertions would fail. The tests cover the two index kinds the parent requirement names and several placements. The other assertions in these tests belong to other requirements.
